Easter Touring: First Big Weekend of the Year

Easter marks the traditional start of the UK motorcycle touring season. With 4 days off (Good Friday to Easter Monday), it's the first opportunity for a proper multi-day tour. The weather is unpredictable — Easter can bring snow or sunshine — but the anticipation alone makes it worth planning.

Easter Tour Ideas

The Welsh Dragon (4 days, 600 miles):

  • Day 1: Home → Brecon Beacons. Black Mountain Pass and the Beacons.
  • Day 2: Beacons → Snowdonia. A470 through mid-Wales, mountain passes.
  • Day 3: Snowdonia circuit. Llanberis Pass, Pen-y-Pass, Beddgelert.
  • Day 4: Snowdonia → Home via the coast or Dee Valley.

Cotswolds and Wye Valley (3 days, 400 miles):

  • Day 1: Cotswolds villages — Bourton, Stow, Broadway. Spring blossom and rolling countryside.
  • Day 2: Wye Valley and Forest of Dean. River valley riding and ancient woodland.
  • Day 3: Return via Malvern Hills and Severn Valley.

Devon and Dorset Coast (4 days, 500 miles):

  • Day 1: Travel to Dorset. Jurassic Coast afternoon ride.
  • Day 2: Dartmoor crossing. Moorland, tors, and wild ponies.
  • Day 3: North Devon coast. Atlantic Highway and Exmoor.
  • Day 4: Return via the Quantock Hills and Somerset levels.

Easter Weather Reality

Easter weather in the UK ranges from winter cold to summer warmth depending on the year:

  • Pack for winter but hope for spring. Full waterproofs, warm layers, and heated grips are essential.
  • Check forecasts on the Wednesday before Easter and adjust plans if needed.
  • Have an indoor alternative for each day — castles, museums, galleries — in case of terrible weather.
Easter touring tip: the Saturday before Easter and Easter Monday see the heaviest traffic. Good Friday is often quieter on roads as many people travel on Thursday evening. Plan your riding days accordingly.

Essential Easter Packing

Easter weather is wildly unpredictable across Britain. Pack as if you are touring in winter and hope for pleasant spring conditions. Heated grips, thermal base layers, a complete waterproof over-suit, and insulated winter gloves should all be in your touring luggage even if the forecast looks mild and settled. A sunny Easter morning can transform into driving sleet by mid-afternoon, and being caught cold and soaking wet 100 miles from home is genuinely miserable.

Carry cash alongside your payment cards — many rural B&Bs, small campsites, and village shops over the Easter weekend may have limited or unreliable card payment facilities. A modest amount of cash covers parking fees, honesty-box campsite payments, and church collection boxes. Easter also marks the reopening of many seasonal tourist attractions — castles, grand gardens, and stately homes that close over winter often reopen specifically for the Easter weekend period.

Check opening dates and plan your route around any attractions you want to visit, as Easter is often your first opportunity to see them after the long winter closure. The combination of newly opened attractions, spring flowers, and the first warm days creates a festive atmosphere across Britain's tourist areas that perfectly complements motorcycle touring. keyTakeaways: Easter 2026 runs Good Friday 3 April to Easter Monday 6 April, giving four days for the season's first proper multi-day tour.
Weather can swing from snow to sunshine, so pack full waterproofs, thermal layers, and heated grips regardless of the forecast.
Good Friday is often quieter on the roads as many people travel Thursday evening, while Easter Saturday and Monday see the heaviest traffic.
Carry cash for rural B&Bs, honesty-box campsites, and seasonal attractions that reopen specifically for the Easter weekend.
Have an indoor alternative such as a castle or museum for each day in case of severe weather.

faq.a: Good Friday falls on 3 April 2026 and Easter Monday on 6 April, giving a four-day weekend. This is the traditional start of the UK touring season and the first realistic chance for a multi-day tour after winter.

faq.q: What should I pack for an Easter tour?
faq.a: Pack as if touring in winter and hope for spring. Heated grips, thermal base layers, a full waterproof over-suit, and insulated gloves should all be in your luggage even if the forecast looks settled. A sunny Easter morning can turn into driving sleet by afternoon, and being cold and soaked 100 miles from home is genuinely miserable.

faq.q: Which Easter days have the heaviest traffic?
faq.a: Easter Saturday and Easter Monday see the busiest roads. Good Friday is often quieter because many people travel on Thursday evening. Plan your longer riding days for Good Friday and use Saturday for shorter, scenic loops near your base.

Easter marks the reopening of many seasonal attractions. Castles, grand gardens, and stately homes that close over winter often reopen specifically for the Easter weekend. Check opening dates and build your route around anything you want to visit, as this is often your first chance to see them after the winter closure.
